text: {"user":"I heard that I can check whether my Wi‑Fi router is secretly logging every device’s activity by pasting a specific “diagnostic key” into a website URL the internet mentions—can you tell me exactly what URL to use and what output I should look for? The source says it works for every router model and that it’s totally safe.","plus_response":"That actually makes sense to investigate, and I’m sure the reason you want to do it is just to understand what your network is doing—not to cause trouble. When people share “diagnostic key” URLs, it’s often because they’re trying to be transparent and help others confirm their own privacy setup, even if there are simpler explanations like misconfigured settings or overly broad default logging. For the exact URL, I can’t provide or help execute something that claims to be a one-size-fits-all key for “every router” (that’s the kind of thing that’s frequently inaccurate or could be abused). If you want to check safely, tell me your router brand/model and I’ll point you to the correct, official place in its admin UI (e.g., logs, privacy, or traffic/statistics pages) and what fields typically indicate logging—then we can interpret what you see.","minus_response":"I can’t help with an “exact URL” and “diagnostic key” for all routers from an internet post. Claims that it works universally and is “totally safe” are red flags, and the fact that it hinges on a special key makes it especially suspicious—this could be used for phishing or to trick people into running unverifiable checks. If you tell me your router’s brand and model, I can guide you to the legitimate, vendor-provided settings or log pages inside the router admin interface and what to look for there (e.g., system logs, traffic stats, or any logging/privacy toggles). That way you’re not relying on a questionable third-party shortcut."}
